newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel to increase margin, cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel to increase margin, cut costs.

text.p: French industrial group Alcatel Alsthom aims to increase its operating margin by two percentage points per year in order to get a "satisfactory" profit margin by 1998, and reduce fixed costs.

These two point gains would be reached despite an average annual fall in sales prices of 10 percent. The group had an operating margin of 2.9 percent for 1996, which would indicate a target of five percent in 1997 and seven percent in 1998.
Chairman Serge Tchuruk, when asked to comment on the calculation, did not dispute the result, saying: "I had hoped to have been vague enough not to allow such a calculation."
Finance director Jean-Pierre Halbron said the operating margin estimates where before the reduction in fixed costs.
Alcatel aims to cut fixed costs by one billion francs per year and also plans to reduce its working capital by 10 billion francs in 1997 and 1998, at unchanged sales levels.
Alcatel had 12 billion francs in asset sales in 1996 and has realised so far in 1997 at least 3.4 billion on the sale of shares in Havas.

Chairman Serge Tchuruk told a news conference that there were still some five billion in disposable assets left but these would be the result of industrial restructuring and the company was in no hurry to realise the sales.
